1.0 INTRODUCTION:

1.1 To define emergency services with law and regulations.

2.0 SCOPE:

2.1 Hospital Management

2.4 Government agencies

3.1 Doctors

4.1 COP-Care of Patients

6.0 REFERENCE:

6.1 NABH : Accreditation Standards For Ayurved Hospitals 2nd Edition April 2016.

7.0 OBJECTIVE ELEMENTS

7.1 Policies and procedure for emergency care are documented

7.2 Policies also address handling of medico-legal cases.

7.3 The patients receive care in consonance with the policies

7.4 Documented policies and procedures guide the triage of patients for initiation of appropriate care.

7.5 Staff is familiar with the policies and trained on the procedures for care of emergency patients.

7.6 Admission or discharge to home or transfer to another organization is also documented.

7.7 In case of discharge to home or transfer to another organization a discharge card shall be given to the patient.

8. 0 PROCESSES

8.1 Hospital provides primary emergency care happening within the hospital as mentioned below according to procedures.

A. SNEHANA (INTERNAL OLEATION)

Safety Precautions

• Care should be taken to avoid excessive heating of sneha dravya.

• For the relaxation of muscles, only gentle pressure has to be applied

Emergency Management

• Abhyanga should stop immediately and symptomatic treatment should be given to the patient.

B. ABHYANGA (EXTERNAL OLEATION / MASSAGE)

Safety Precautions

• Care should be taken to avoid excessive heating of sneha dravya.

• For the relaxation of muscles, only gentle pressure has to be applied

Emergency Management

• Abhyanga should stop immediately and symptomatic treatment should be given to patients.

C. BASHPA SWEDA (STEAM BATH)

Safety Precautions

• Direct contact of steam with body parts should be avoided.

• Excessive heating and excessive perspiration is avoided

Emergency Management

• Fainting – Sprinkle cold water on the face; apply suitable oil, Chandrakala ras 250mg 2 Tablets and Lakshmivilas Ras 250mg 2 tablets internally.

• Burns – Apply Madhu (Honey), Ghrita (Ghee), Ghritakumari (Aloe vera) or suitable treatment.

D. VAMANA (THERAPEUTIC EMESIS)

Safety Precautions

• Medicines should be given in proper quantity based on age, strength, constitution, and season.

• Avoid overstraining the patient during Vamana.

Emergency Management

• Excessive vomiting / Frothy vomitus: Stop procedure, give cooling dryers like Yashtimadhu Phanta, hydrate with glucose water/ORS.

• Hematemesis: Stop procedure, apply ice pack, give Tab. Praval panchamrut, start IV and refer if needed.

• Severe weakness/dizziness: Supine position, elevate legs, IV dextrose, monitor vitals.

• Uncontrolled vomiting or collapse: Initiate BLS and refer to SMHRC Emergency Unit.

E. BASTI (MEDICATED ENEMA)

Safety Precautions

• Care during insertion of Basti netra in anus.

• Observe Niruha Basti pratyagamana kala (45–60 min).

Emergency Management

• Local anal injury: Treat with local care.

• GIT symptoms: Manage pain, vomiting symptomatically.

• Rare generalized symptoms (murchha, angamarda): Symptomatic treatment

F. NASYA (NASAL INSUFFLATIONS)

Safety Precautions

• Proper selection of drug and dose based on patient condition.

Emergency Management

• Headache, giddiness, running nose – Stop procedure, symptomatic management.

G. KAYA SEKA (PIZHICHIL)

Safety Precautions

• Avoid painful inflammatory conditions or acute fever.

• Avoid overheating of oil. • Monitor vitals.

Emergency Management

• Fainting – Stop, keep head low, IV Dextrose.

H. SHASHTIKA SHALI PINDA SWEDA (NAVARAKIZHI)

Safety Precautions

• Prevent burns and dermal injuries.

• Avoid overheating pottali.

• Monitor vitals.

Emergency Management

• Fainting – Stop, head low, IV Dextrose.

I. AVAGAHA SWEDA (SITZ BATH)

Safety Precautions

• Avoid overheating of water.

• Prevent burns.

• Monitor vitals.

Emergency Management

• Fainting – Stop, head low, IV Dextrose.

J. UPANAHA (POULTICE)

Safety Precautions

• Prevent burns or dermal injury.

• Monitor vitals.

Emergency Management

• Burn injury – Apply Aloe Vera.

K. PATRA PINDA SWEDA

Safety Precautions

• Avoid painful inflammatory conditions and fever.

• Avoid overheating pottali.

• Monitor vitals.

Emergency Management

• Burn injury – Apply Aloe Vera.

L. CHURNA SWEDA

Safety Precautions

• Avoid overheating of pottali.

• Monitor vitals.

Emergency Management

• Burn injury – Apply Aloe Vera.

M. SHIRODHARA

Safety Precautions

• Prevent burns and protect eyes/ears from dravya.

• Monitor vitals.

Emergency Management

• Burn injury – Apply Aloe Vera.

• Headache – Stop procedure.

N. SHIROLEPANA

Safety Precautions

• Monitor vitals.

Emergency Management

• Headache – Stop procedure.

O. SHIRO BASTI

Safety Precautions

• Avoid burns, seal basti yantra properly.

• Monitor vitals.

Emergency Management

• Burn injury – Apply Aloe Vera.

• Headache – Stop procedure.

P. KATI BASTI

Safety Precautions

• Avoid overheating of oil.

• Prevent dermal burns.

• Monitor vitals.

Emergency Management

• Burn injury – Apply Aloe Vera.

Q. URO BASTI

Safety Precautions

• Avoid overheating of oil.

• Prevent dermal burns.

• Monitor vitals.

Emergency Management

• Burn injury – Apply Aloe Vera.

R. AGNIKARMA

Safety Precautions

• Do not perform on an empty stomach; avoid marma points.

• Check dosha, disease, and ritu before starting.

• Proper assessment before applying Shalaka.

• Maintain hygiene post-procedure.

Emergency Management

• Burns – Apply sterile ghee, Aloe Vera, Shatadhauta ghrita.

• Pain – Use sandalwood paste, medicated oils.

• Fainting – Supine position, fresh air, cold water, sweet fluids.

• Infection – Maintain asepsis, use antiseptic herbal pastes.

S. RAKTAMOKSHANA

Safety Precautions

• Avoid anemia, hypotension, or bleeding disorders.

• Use sterilized instruments, aseptic techniques.

Emergency Management

• Excessive bleeding – Use styptic herbs, cooling decoctions.

• Fainting – Supine, elevate legs, give glucose water.

• Infection – Apply antiseptic pastes or oils.

• Allergy (Leech) – Remove leech, apply turmeric, give antihistamines.

• Severe reaction – Refer to Apex Wellness Hospital

Other emergencies mentioned below will be referred to Apex Wellness Hospital. Nashik

8.1.1Respiratory:

8.1.1.1 Acute respiratory failure (PaO2 < 60 mm Hg).

8.1.1.2 Respiratory rate > 30 breaths/minute and <8 breadth/minute.

81.1.2.3 Patients requiring ventilator support (invasive or non-invasive).

8.1.1.2.4 Pulmonary embolism with hemodynamic instability.

8.1.1.2.5 Massive Hemoptysis

8.1.1.2.6 SPO2 saturation below 85

8.1.2 Surgical:

8.1.2.1 Post-operative patients requiring hemodynamic monitoring, ventilator support or extensive nursing care.

8.1.2.2 Patients with surgical abdomen requiring preoperative fluid and/or electrolyte resuscitation.

8.1.2..3 Trauma with significant injury to thoracic / abdominal organs requiring surgical intervention.

8.1.3 Renal:

8.1.3.1 Patients who have acute renal failure with accompanying respiratory or hemodynamic components require close monitoring & respiratory/ hemodynamic support.

8.1.3..2 Significant acidosis or alkalosis.

8.1.4 Drug Ingestion and overdose:

8.1.4..1 Drug ingestion with significantly altered mental status & inadequate airway protection / hemodynamic instability.

8.1.4.2 Seizures following drug ingestion

8.1.5 Endocrine:

8.1.5.1 Diabetic ketoacidosis is complicated by hemodynamic instability, altered mental status, respiratory insufficiency, or severe acidosis.

8.1.5.2 Thyroid storm or myxedema coma with hemodynamic instability.

8.1.5..3 other endocrine problems such as adrenal crisis with hemodynamic instability

8.1.6 Road Traffic Accident:

8.1.6.1 Head injury Caused by road traffic accident

8.1.6.2 Fracture

8.1.7 Miscellaneous:

8.1.7.1 Environmental injuries (lighting, near drowning, hyperthermia or hypothermia).

8.1.7.2 Any other clinical conditions requiring ICU level nursing care.

8.1.7..3 Suicidal gestures including partial hanging, drug overdoses and other selfinflicted injuries.

8.2 Other:

8.2.1 All cases of accidents, burns, assaults, alleged suicide or homicide, poisoning, road traffic accident, rape, drowning, etc shall be registered as medico legal cases (MLC).

8.2.2 All cases registered as medico legal in hospitals where he/she reported first must also be registered as Medico legal and the outside Medico Legal Case number recorded on the case file.

8.2.3 Any case of a cognizable offense as mentioned above even if brought at a later date by the police must be informed and the case registered as medico legal.

8.2.4 When a case identified as medico legal is brought to Casualty, the Casualty Medical Officer shall provide medical care as required.

8.2.5 Casualty Medical Officer shall inform the Hingna police station. The time of call and the police personnel spoken to shall also be documented.

8.2.6 Medico Legal Case Form shall be filled by Casualty Medical Officer in duplicate (one copy for Medical Records Dept. and one for the Police) Medico Legal Case report shall be completed and signed as soon as possible after the patient arrives in Emergency and in all cases before the Casualty Medical Officer goes off duty. Casualty Medical Officers shall not be relieved until Medico Legal Case reports for patients managed in the tenure of duty are completed.

8.2.7 An entry must be made in the Medico Legal Case intimation report in case the patient is already registered as Medico legal in another hospital.

8.3 Reference: -Hospital treatment manual

8.4.1 Triage shall be done only by qualified/trained individuals. This should be based on good clinical practices.

8.4.2 Through regular modules, held for both Doctors and nursing staff, by trained staff in the technique of Triaging.

8.4.3 The policy of prioritizing patients is based on the urgency of their individual need for medical care.

8.4.4 Under normal working conditions, patients shall be triaged and allotted beds in the ER as per the urgency of their medical needs.

8.4.5 During external disasters (Code Red) patients shall be triaged as Red, Yellow, Green and Black according to the following criteria:

a. Red: First priority, most urgent, life-threatening shock or hypoxia is present or imminent, but the patient can be stabilized and, if given immediate care, shall probably survive.

Examples Red:

• Compromised airway

• Respiratory arrest or severe respiratory distress or SpO2 < 90

• Cardiac arrest

• Hypotension (BP < 90 mm Hg)

• Trauma patient who is unresponsive or requires immediate fluid resuscitation

• Overdose with a respiratory rate of 6.

• Severe bradycardia or tachycardia with signs of hypo-perfusion.

• Chest pain

• Anaphylactic reaction.

• Baby that is flaccid.

• Hypoglycemia with a change in mental status.

b. Yellow: Second Priority, Urgent, Injuries have systemic implications or effects, but the patient is not yet in life threatening shock or hypoxia; although systemic decline shall ensue and given appropriate care, the patient seems able to withstand a 45 to 60 minute wait without immediate risk.

Examples of Yellow: Following diagnosis with stable blood pressure. Tachycardia / dyspnea may or may not be present

• Acute abdominal pain

• Gastro-intestinal bleeding

• Acute arterial occlusion

• Fever in immuno-compromised patients

• Testicular torsion

• Acute renal failure

• Ectopic pregnancy

• Spontaneous abortion

• Rule out meningitis

• Acute Cerebro-vascular accident

• Vomiting / diarrhea in children

• Acute asthmatic attack

• Pleural effusion

• Spontaneous pneumothorax

• Road traffic accident with transient loss of consciousness.

c. Green: Third Priority, Non-urgent, Injuries are localized and without immediate systemic implications; with a minimum of care, the patient generally does not deteriorate for up to several hours.

d. Black: Dead, No distinction can be made between clinical and biologic death in a mass casualty incident, and any unresponsive patient who has no spontaneous ventilation or circulation is classified as dead.

8.5 All the staff working in the area are oriented to the policies and practices through training/documents. Staff is trained in BLS.

8.6 Registration of the patient will be done at the registration counter. Interns will divert/narrate patients according to his/her symptoms The registration time is 10 minutes. The exceptions are:-

• During peak hours- 9 am to 1 pm.

• When there is shortage of staff due to circumstances beyond control. The waiting time in the OPD is half an hour for booked patients. The exceptions are:-

• If the doctor is called on to an emergency.

• If the doctor is held up in surgery or similar unavoidable procedures if there are more patients with no prior appointment.

8.6.1 In patients registration

a. The patient obtains admission from the concerned doctor.

b. The registration process at the registration counter does not exceed 10 minutes except during peak hours 9 am – 1 pm.

c. Consultation by respective doctor and initiation of necessary investigations/ treatment.

d. Register the patient.

e. Identify the specialty needed, if any.

f. Identify medico-legal cases. If so, arrange for formalities through Casualty.

8.6.2 Admission process

• Written order by the treating Doctor

• Admission registration.

• Allotment of room/ ward

• All admissions are documented.

8.7 Process to Transfer to another Organization

• During non-availability of beds, patients will be referred to Apex Wellness Hospital or if patient requests another facility, to that specific facility.

• Unstable patients are transferred to other facilities by an equipped ambulance accompanied by a doctor and or trained personnel as indicated.

• Stable patients can avail the facility of the organization's ambulance or arrangements will be made for other ambulance service or the patients can obtain private vehicles of their choice.

• The patient will be adequately assisted by the hospital staff – nurses and ward boys/Aayahs till the place and point of transfer/Ambulance.

• The summary given to the patient contains the information of condition and treatment given, for IPD and LAMA (DAMA). The institution to which the patient is referred will be contacted by the concerned doctor with a view to discuss with them the patient’s condition, bed availability etc.

8.8 In case of discharge to home or transfer to another organization a discharge note shall be given to the patients per hospital standard format.
